body:
I'm not convinced that the reasons outlined are sufficient for making such a codebase wide change, and breaking compatibility for thirdparty modules.

`print_verbose` is meant to be related to `print_line` and `print_error`. Making it upper case breaks this familiarity, for a reason that's technically just an implementation detail.

I'd prefer we make it a global inline function like `print_line` instead of a macro if we really want to change something.

> I'd prefer we make it a global inline function like `print_line` instead of a macro if we really want to change something.

Making it be a normal function would also resolve the issue as far as I'm concerned

> So the reason it's a macro is to avoid processing its String parameter if we're not actually printing verbose stuff:
> 
> ```c++
> // This version avoids processing the text to be printed until it actually has to be printed, saving some CPU usage.
> #define print_verbose(m_text)             \
> 	{                                     \
> 		if (is_print_verbose_enabled()) { \
> 			print_line(m_text);           \
> 		}                                 \
> 	}
> ```

An `inline` function would do the same, right?
The only way to avoid evaluating parameters is to make it a macro instead of a function.

The name conflict part of the issue has been solved by #102062.

Now, there's still merit in discussing whether we want to make the macro `PRINT_VERBOSE` for consistency with usual macro naming style, or keep it lower case for consistency with `print_line` and `print_error` functions.

I'm personally more for the latter, but I wouldn't strongly oppose the former if there's consensus that it's the way to go.

> The name conflict part of the issue has been solved by #102062.

It fixes it on the Godot side. We still kind of have it on the godot-cpp side, although, we're working around it by making it a function, and maybe have a couple other options to work around it if we want `print_verbose()` to be a macro there too.

> Now, there's still merit in discussing whether we want to make the macro `PRINT_VERBOSE` for consistency with usual macro naming style, or keep it lower case for consistency with `print_line` and `print_error` functions.

There are semantic differences between functions and macros, so I'd personally be for `PRINT_VERBOSE` so it's clear that it's a macro, avoiding any confusion. That said, this isn't a very big problem :-)

I like the idea of ​​unifying naming, but we have many other macros named in lowercase (notably `memnew`, `unlikely`, and their counterparts). Do you suggest renaming them as well? Perhaps `print_verbose` is specifically named this way to be consistent with `print_line`, `print_error`, and so on?

@dalexeev I do not want to force a global convention on everything, but with `PRINT_VERBOSE` there is a naming conflict with the `print_verbose` function if it is kept as lowercase. This is worked around already in godot-cpp by making it a function, but then it's not a macro anymore, so the parameters are always evaluated even if verbose printing is not enabled.
